title: The open-complement condition from the direct-image input
statement:
Let $k$ be the algebraic closure of a finite field, let $d\in\mathbf Z_{\geq0}$, let $T$ be a finite-type $k$-scheme of Krull dimension at most $d$ [def-weil-finite-type-morphism; def-kun-topological-krull-dimension], and let $j:V\hookrightarrow T$ be a quasi-compact open immersion [def-weil-open-immersion]. Let $A$ be a finite commutative ring annihilated by a power of a prime $\ell\neq\operatorname{char}(k)$. Then the pair $(V,T)$ satisfies the open-complement condition at $A$ of [def-exc-open-complement-bound] with $c=2d$.
Independently of the general argument, the condition holds in dimension zero because an open immersion into a zero-dimensional Noetherian scheme (locally Noetherian [pqf-def-locnoeth] and quasi-compact) is also a closed immersion [def-weil-closed-immersion] and its direct image is exact extension by zero, preserving constructibility. In dimension at most one, [thm-exc-curve-open-dimension-general] and [thm-exc-curve-open-constructible-general] give the independent vanishing and constructibility assertions (with vanishing already for $q>1$).

proof.text: The algebraic closure $k$ is separably closed: every nonconstant polynomial has a root, hence so does every separable one, as required by [def-pc-separably-closed]. Choose $r\geq1$ such that $\ell^r A=0$, and set $N=\ell^r$. Enlarging an initially given exponent to at least one does not change annihilation, including when $A$ is the zero ring. Since $\ell\neq\operatorname{char}(k)$, $N$ is prime to the characteristic. Every section $m$ of every $A$-module sheaf satisfies $Nm=(N1_A)m=0$.

source.place: Proof, first sentence: separably closed base and coefficient annihilator

proof.text: The quasi-compact open immersion $j$ is of finite type by [lem-weil-pbc-qc-open-immersion-finite-type]. We also need its source to be finite type over $k$, and check this separately. By [def-weil-finite-type-morphism], $T$ has a finite affine open cover with finitely generated $k$-algebras. The inverse image of each member under $j$ is quasi-compact; hence $V$ is quasi-compact, since the finitely many finite subcovers of any open cover combine into a finite subcover. Identify $V$ with its open image in $T$ by [def-weil-open-immersion]. By [lem-pqf-finite-affine-cover-qc-open], this image has a finite cover by affine opens of $T$. Applying [lem-weil-pbc-lft-affine-pairs] to $T\to\operatorname{Spec}k$ shows that the coordinate algebra of each member is finitely generated over $k$. This finite affine cover witnesses that $V$ is finite type over $k$.

source.place: Tags 01T0 and 01T2 (lemma-locally-finite-type-characterize); geometry needed for the imported proof constructibility clause

proof.text: The identification of $V$ with an open subspace of $T$ in [def-weil-open-immersion] lets us apply [lem-weil-pbc-open-subspace-dimension-monotone] with $U'=V$ and $U=T$. Thus $\dim V\leq\dim T\leq d$. The same open-subspace inequality will be applied to $V\times_TU\subseteq U$ in step 8; the etale dimension comparison needed there is proved separately in step 7.

source.place: Remark after Tag 0055 (definition-Krull): dimension of open subspaces

proof.text: Apply [thm-exc-direct-image-input-holds] with the separably closed field $k$, the integer $N$ and the finite commutative ring $A$. Clause (1) of [def-exc-direct-image-input] applies to $j$ by step 2: both schemes and the morphism are finite type. It gives constructibility of $R^qj_*F$ for every constructible $A$-module sheaf $F$ and every $q\geq0$. No exceptional inverse image, purity or preservation theorem is used.

source.place: Proof, first three sentences: clause (1) of the direct-image input applied to j

proof.text: For $q<0$, apply [lem-weil-pbc-derived-functor-negative-vanishing] with $b=0$, $L=F[0]$ and $v=j_*$. The module-sheaf categories on $V$ and $T$ are Grothendieck abelian by [lem-weil-pbc-module-sheaves-grothendieck-abelian], and $j_*$ is additive and left exact by [def-weil-pbc-direct-image]. The conclusion is $R^qj_*F=0$. The zero sheaf is constructible: use the one stratum $T$, with its constant finite zero module, in [def-weil-pbc-constructible-complexes] (or the empty partition when $T$ is empty). Together with step 4 this supplies every integer degree required by the open-complement condition.

source.place: Tag 05TC (lemma-negative-vanishing), part (1), applied to a sheaf in degree zero

proof.text: Fix an affine etale object $u:U\to T$. We first prove that $U$ is finite type over $k$, rather than assume this for arbitrary etale objects. By [def-weil-etale-morphism], $u$ is locally of finite presentation. The explicit charts in [def-sbc-locally-finite-presentation] cover $U$ by affine opens $E_a=\operatorname{Spec} B_a$ mapping into affine opens $D_a=\operatorname{Spec} R_a$ of $T$, with $B_a$ finitely presented, hence finitely generated, over $R_a$. By [lem-weil-pbc-lft-affine-pairs] applied to $T\to\operatorname{Spec}k$, each $R_a$ is finitely generated over $k$. If $r_1,\ldots,r_m$ generate $R_a/k$ and $b_1,\ldots,b_n$ generate $B_a/R_a$, their images together generate $B_a/k$: expand every coefficient of a polynomial in the $b_i$ as a polynomial in the $r_j$. Thus each $B_a$ is finitely generated over $k$. By [lem-weil-pbc-affine-scheme-qcqs], $U$ is quasi-compact, so finitely many of these $E_a$ cover $U$. This is exactly the finite affine covering criterion of [def-weil-finite-type-morphism] for $U/k$.

source.place: Tags 02GI (definition-etale), 01TP (definition-finite-presentation) and 01T2; the affine-neighbourhood restriction in the blueprint vanishing paragraph

proof.text: For the same affine etale $U\to T$, prove $\dim U\leq\dim T$. At $z\in U$ choose affine neighbourhoods $\operatorname{Spec}B\subseteq U$ and $\operatorname{Spec}R\subseteq T$ around $z$ and $t=u(z)$ such that $R\to B$ is etale, as in the affine-chart characterization in [def-weil-etale-morphism]. Write $\mathfrak q$ for $z$ and $\mathfrak p$ for its image. Clause (c) of [lem-weil-pbc-affine-open-stalk-localization] identifies $\mathcal O_{U,z}$ with $B_{\mathfrak q}$ and $\mathcal O_{T,t}$ with $R_{\mathfrak p}$, and [lem-sc-etale-local-dimension] gives equality of their Krull dimensions. Now [lem-pc-scheme-dimension-local-rings] gives $\dim U=\sup_{z\in U}\dim\mathcal O_{U,z}\leq\sup_{t\in T}\dim\mathcal O_{T,t}=\dim T\leq d$. This inequality includes empty $U$, when the first supremum is $-\infty$. No dimension assertion about a strict henselization is used.

Put $W=V\times_TU$. By [lem-weil-pbc-open-immersion-base-change] its projection to $U$ is an open immersion, and by [lem-pc-quasi-compact-base-change] that projection is quasi-compact. Since $U$ is affine, the definition of a quasi-compact morphism in [def-weil-finite-type-morphism] says that $W$ is quasi-compact. Identify it with its open image in $U$ using [def-weil-open-immersion]. The finite affine cover supplied by [lem-pqf-finite-affine-cover-qc-open] has coordinate rings finitely generated over $k$ by [lem-weil-pbc-lft-affine-pairs] applied to the finite-type structure map of $U$ established in step 6. Thus $W$ is finite type over $k$ by [def-weil-finite-type-morphism]. The open-subspace inequality [lem-weil-pbc-open-subspace-dimension-monotone] and step 7 give $\dim W\leq\dim U\leq d$. The empty open is covered by the empty finite family, so no nonemptiness assumption is introduced.

source.place: Tags 01JY (lemma-base-change-immersion) and 01K5 (lemma-quasi-compact-preserved-base-change); Morphisms 01T2; Topology 0055 following remark

proof.text: Fix an arbitrary $A$-module sheaf $M$ on $V$ and an integer $q>2d$, and write $G$ for its underlying abelian sheaf. Since $d\geq0$, $q$ is positive. The morphism $W=V\times_TU\to V$ is etale by [lem-weil-pbc-etale-base-change-finite-limits]. By [lem-weil-pbc-etale-inverse-image-restriction], the restricted abelian sheaf has section groups $G(Z\to W\to V)$ on every etale $Z\to W$. Step 1 kills each such group by the same positive integer $N$, so the restriction is torsion, including for nonconstructible $M$. Apply clause (2) of [def-exc-direct-image-input], proved by [thm-exc-direct-image-input-holds], with $K=k$ and this $W$. Its finite-type and dimension hypotheses are steps 6-8, and its characteristic hypothesis is step 1. Thus $H^q(W,G|_W)=0$ for every affine etale $U\to T$. By [sbc-lem-higher-direct-image-presheaf], the abelian higher direct image $R^qj_*G$ is the sheafification of $P_q:U\mapsto H^q(V\times_TU,G|)$; we have proved that $P_q$ is zero on all affine objects. This is a statement about the cohomology presheaf, not an identification of the sections of its sheafification with those cohomology groups.

source.place: Tag 03Q8 (lemma-higher-direct-images); Tag 03S2 restriction formula; item blueprint vanishing paragraph, application of clause (2)

proof.text: To conclude that $P_q^\#=0$, use the affine cover statement [lem-weil-pbc-affine-etale-essentially-small-cover]. For any object $Z$ and any $s\in P_q(Z)$, choose a cover by affine etale objects $U_i\to Z$. For any morphism $\alpha:P_q\to H$ to an abelian sheaf $H$, naturality gives $\alpha_Z(s)|_{U_i}=\alpha_{U_i}(s|_{U_i})=0$, since $P_q(U_i)=0$. The equalizer condition in [def-weil-pbc-abelian-etale-sheaves] makes the restriction maps jointly injective, so $\alpha_Z(s)=0$. Thus every such $\alpha$ is zero. Apply this with $H=P_q^\#$ and the unit $\theta:P_q\to P_q^\#$ of [def-weil-pbc-sheafification]. The identity and the zero endomorphism of $P_q^\#$ have the same composite with $\theta$; the uniqueness in that definition implies $\operatorname{id}_{P_q^\#}=0$. Therefore $P_q^\#$, and hence $R^qj_*G$, is the zero abelian sheaf. This proves directly the affine-neighbourhood vanishing used by the imported stalk argument, without invoking an unrecorded strict-local continuity formula.

source.place: Tags 021B and 04HR (affine objects cover); Sites 00WH (sheafification universal property); explicit elementary local-zero argument

proof.text: Apply [lem-sbc-higher-direct-image-forget-comparison] with $\Lambda=A$, $h=j$, $F=M$ and the integer $q$. It identifies the underlying abelian sheaf of the module higher direct image $R^qj_*M$ with the zero abelian higher direct image $R^qj_*G$ from steps 9-10. Thus every section group of $R^qj_*M$ has just its zero element; its module structure is uniquely that of the zero module and all restriction maps are the unique zero maps. It is therefore the zero $A$-module sheaf. This holds for every $M$ and every $q>2d$ and uses no assertion that forgetting coefficients preserves injective objects.

source.place: Tags 03FD (lemma-cohomology-modules-abelian-agree, including every object) and 072W (lemma-higher-direct-images); acyclic-resolution comparison

proof.text: Steps 4 and 5 give the constructibility clause in every integer degree; steps 6-11 give the vanishing clause for every $A$-module sheaf. These are exactly the two clauses of [def-exc-open-complement-bound], with the nonnegative integer $c=2d$. This proves the general assertion. If $T$ or $V$ is empty the same argument applies; in the empty source category the sheaf is zero and all its direct images are zero.

source.place: Proof, final sentence: the open-complement condition with c=2d

proof.text: For the independent dimension-zero argument, $\operatorname{Spec}k$ is Noetherian: a field has only the ideals $(0)$ and $(1)$ and its spectrum has one point. Hence [lem-weil-pbc-finite-type-over-noetherian] makes $T$ Noetherian. If $\dim T\leq0$, [lem-sc-zero-dim-noetherian-finite-discrete] says that $|T|$ is finite discrete, including the empty case. Thus the open image of $j$ is also closed. By [def-weil-open-immersion], it is an open subscheme isomorphic to $V$; its inclusion is also a closed immersion by [def-weil-closed-immersion]: it is a homeomorphism onto a closed subset, and the structure-sheaf map is surjective, being the identity on $V$ and the map to the zero sheaf on the complementary open. Put $W=T\setminus V$, with its open subscheme structure. The two disjoint open subschemes glue back to $T=V\amalg W$: maps defined on them glue uniquely, since their intersection is empty.

For this clopen decomposition, [lem-weil-pbc-etale-sheaf-clopen-product] identifies abelian sheaves on $T$ with pairs of sheaves on $V,W$. The same identification carries $A$-module sheaves to pairs of $A$-module sheaves: an $A$-action consists of additive endomorphisms indexed by $A$ satisfying the ring identities, and both morphisms and these identities are recovered componentwise. A local section of the constant sheaf $A_T$ is locally represented by elements of $A$, so the actions of those elements define its action locally and glue uniquely; this verifies that the componentwise description is one of $A_T$-modules, not merely additive groups with selected endomorphisms. By the evaluation formula of [def-weil-pbc-direct-image], $j_*M$ corresponds to $(M,0)$: its restriction on $V$ is $M$, and on $W$ all fibre products with $V$ are empty. Kernels and cokernels of maps of pairs are componentwise, so $M\mapsto(M,0)$ is exact and additive. The categories have enough injectives by [lem-weil-pbc-module-sheaves-enough-injectives]; [lem-sc-exact-functor-higher-derived-vanishing] therefore gives $R^qj_*M=0$ for $q>0$. To identify degree zero explicitly, choose an injective resolution $0\to F\to I^0\to I^1\to\cdots$. Exactness of $j_*$ makes $0\to j_*F\to j_*I^0\to j_*I^1\to\cdots$ exact; taking degree-zero cohomology in the resolution formula of [def-weil-pbc-direct-image] gives $R^0j_*F=\ker(j_*I^0\to j_*I^1)\cong j_*F$. Negative degrees vanish by the purely homological argument of step 5, which does not use the general finiteness input. Finally, if $F$ is constructible on $V$, keep its finite stratification and add $W$, on which the extension is the constant zero module. These are locally closed constructible strata of $T$ because $V,W$ are clopen; thus [def-weil-pbc-constructible-complexes] proves constructibility of $j_*F$, and the zero higher images are constructible too. The condition holds with $c=0$, independently of steps 4 and 6-11.

source.place: Clopen decomposition as in the proof of Tag 0A5B (lemma-constant-smooth-statements); exact-functor consequence in literature/stacks-project/derived.tex, Tag 015F (lemma-right-derived-exact-functor)

proof.text: For the independent curve assertion, suppose $\dim T\leq1$. The same $k$ is the algebraic closure of a finite field. The prime $\ell$ is invertible on $T$: its nonzero element in the field $k$ has an inverse, whose image in every $k$-algebra of functions is an inverse. Thus [thm-exc-curve-open-dimension-general] applies to $T,j,A$ and gives $R^qj_*M=0$ already for $q>1$, for every $A$-module sheaf $M$. The companion [thm-exc-curve-open-constructible-general] gives constructibility in every degree. By [def-exc-open-complement-bound], these give the condition with $c=1$, and hence with $c=2d$ whenever $d\geq1$. For $d=0$ use steps 13-14, whose stronger $c=0$ bound includes $q=1$. This proves the low-dimensional assertions without invoking the general direct-image input or the general affine-neighbourhood vanishing argument.

source.place: Final sentence of statement: independent dimension-zero and curve computations

split_report.summary: Repaired return F1 by removing the unavailable relative-torsion theorem from the proof and expanding its use into affine-etale finite-type geometry, local-ring dimension comparison, the torsion bound of the existing direct-image input, sheafification on an affine cover, and the module/abelian higher-direct-image comparison, all with available source passages. Retained the coefficient-domain correction and independent low-dimensional arguments. Fifteen steps, no new nodes.
split_report.blueprint: Steps 1-5 realize the constructibility paragraph. Steps 6-11 expand the vanishing paragraph by proving its affine-etale finite-type and dimension assertions and applying clause (2) to the cohomology presheaf. Step 10 proves the local-zero sheafification argument explicitly; it computes the same vanishing as the blueprint stalk-colimit argument without needing strict-local continuity. Step 12 assembles the condition. Steps 13-15 prove the final independent dimension-zero and curve clauses. Chapter and unit routes are retained.
